comments.note: BuildConfirmationMessage() iterates DiffLines twice (once for removedCount, once for insertedCount) using Count(). For the expected scale of a plugins list this is negligible, but a single-pass approach could marginally reduce allocations if performance became a concern in future. Not a defect.

The BuildConfirmationMessage_RiskyChanges_IncludesRemovedCount test asserts substring presence ('2 removed mod(s)' and '1 inserted mod'). This is appropriately loose — it avoids coupling tests to the full formatted string — but reviewers should be aware the test does not assert the surrounding template text from ConfirmUpdateMessage_RiskyChanges. Low risk given the locale completeness tests already guard all locale strings.

comments.note: DiffDialogViewModel.cs Dispose(): The DiffLines.CollectionChanged -= OnDiffCollectionChanged statement was duplicated — once inside the null-guard early-return branch and once in the main branch. Since both branches executed the same unsubscription before exiting, the copy inside the early-return was dead code (the return guaranteed the second copy never ran). Fixed by hoisting the unsubscription before the null guard and removing both duplicates. Behavior is identical; no test changes required.

BuildConfirmationMessage() double-passes DiffLines with two Count() calls (one for removedCount, one for insertedCount). At the scale of a plugins list this is negligible, and the clarity of two named counts outweighs the marginal allocation cost. A single-pass approach (e.g., iterating once and branching on ChangeType) is available if performance profiling ever flags this path, but it is not warranted now. Noting for future awareness only.

[documentation-forward] BuildConfirmationMessage() has a summary XML doc comment but no <returns> or <remarks> element documenting the null-return contract (safe-only changes → null, risky changes → formatted string). Adding a <returns> tag would make the contract self-documenting at the call site and in IDE tooltips, especially important since the method is internal and the null signal is load-bearing for the confirmation-dialog branch in UpdateReferenceWithConfirmationAsync().
